title: Single source of truth for sense names in analysisService
story: As a developer, I want only one list of sense names in analysisService.ts so that adding or removing a sense only requires one change.
acceptance_criteria: The seven sense names appear in exactly one place in analysisService.ts
The validator and the Sense type remain consistent with each other
All existing tests continue to pass

title: Replace hardcoded colors with named constants
story: As a developer, I want all colors in the codebase to be defined as named constants so that the codebase is more readable and maintainable.
acceptance_criteria: All hardcoded hex and RGB color values in production code are replaced with named constants
All inline style color values in production code are replaced with named constants
Named constants use a semantic naming scheme (e.g. TEXT_WARNING, BACKGROUND_PRIMARY)
No hardcoded hex or RGB color values remain in any non-test file

title: Storybook stories for Button, RadioGroup, and TextArea components
story: As a developer, I want reusable Button, RadioGroup, and TextArea components with Storybook stories for all used states so that styling is centralized and visually reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Button component exists with default and disabled states
A reusable RadioGroup component exists supporting multiple options with one selectable, with default, selected, and disabled states
A reusable TextArea component exists with default, with-text, and disabled states
Each component state has a dedicated Storybook story
Stories are visual-only — no interaction tests

title: Add human verification gate to ticket-do command
story: As a developer, I want the ticket-do command to pause and ask me to verify before closing a ticket when automated tests are insufficient, so that tickets are never closed without appropriate sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do explicitly distinguishes between tickets that can be closed on passing tests alone and those requiring human verification
When human verification is required, the agent presents testing instructions directly in chat and waits for user confirmation before closing
The agent never leaves testing instructions in code, story files, or comments

title: Add plan re-confirmation step on plan changes in ticket-do
story: As a developer, I want the agent to re-confirm the updated plan with me whenever the plan changes mid-execution, so that I always have visibility and approval before implementation continues.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do instructs the agent to re-present the full updated plan whenever a change is made mid-execution
The agent waits for explicit user confirmation before continuing after a plan change
The re-confirmation step is identical in form to the initial plan confirmation step

title: Groom tickets interactively during sprint-start
story: As a developer, I want each ticket to be groomed interactively as it is pulled into the sprint, so that all sprint tickets are well-scoped and clearly defined before work begins.
acceptance_criteria: sprint-start walks through each candidate ticket one at a time before adding it to the sprint
For each ticket, the agent reviews the story and acceptance criteria, flags any inconsistencies, ambiguities, or scope questions, and presents findings to the user
The user can accept the ticket as-is, edit it based on agent findings, or defer it back to the backlog
Groomed tickets have a clear problem statement understandable to both human and agent without reading the codebase

title: Make story command implementation-agnostic
story: As a developer, I want the story command to focus purely on user-facing problems and acceptance criteria, so that stories are not polluted with implementation details.
acceptance_criteria: The story command explicitly instructs the agent not to read the codebase
The story command explicitly instructs the agent not to include implementation details in the story or acceptance criteria
Acceptance criteria are written from a user or product perspective, not a technical one

title: Add closed ticket status and close-ticket command
story: As a developer, I want to close a ticket without completing programming work, so that I can track intentional decisions to skip or abandon a ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A 'closed' status is a valid terminal status alongside 'done'
A close-ticket command exists that sets a ticket's status to 'closed' and prompts the user for an optional reason
Closed tickets are treated as terminal — they are not pulled into future sprints
sprint-close and retro commands handle closed tickets appropriately

title: Replace LLM-driven verbatim field entry in ticket-do with explicit instruction
story: As a developer, I want verbatim text I provide to be placed into ticket fields exactly as given, without the agent interpreting or acting on it, so that data entry is reliable.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do explicitly instructs the agent to treat user-provided verbatim text as inert data to be transcribed, not as instructions to act on
The agent asks for confirmation before taking any action when the user is in the middle of providing field values
